Distance Between Strings

AlgorithmsCountingLogic
Game: How different are two words? Count the places where they differ, or the fewest letter changes that turn one into the other.
How to play: Type two words, pick a way of measuring, and press Do it!
    Look for the math

    A spelling checker offers the words "nearest" to the one you mistyped. That needs a distance between strings: a number that is 0 only for equal strings, the same both ways round, and obeys the triangle inequality D(s, t) ≤ D(s, r) + D(r, t).

    Hamming distance

    For strings of the same length, the Hamming distance H(s, t) counts the places where they differ. Changing s into t by way of r can never need fewer changes than going straight there, which is the triangle inequality.

    Levenshtein distance

    The Levenshtein distance also allows inserting and deleting letters. Fill a table: d(i, 0) = i, d(0, j) = j, and

    d(i, j) = min( d(i−1, j) + 1, d(i, j−1) + 1, d(i−1, j−1) + r(si, tj) )

    where r is 0 for equal letters and 1 otherwise. The three terms are: delete si, insert tj, or replace si by tj if needed. The corner of the table is the fewest edits that turn one string into the other. The highlighted path shows one such way. The logic test checked the table against a search over all edits for every pair of a-b strings up to length 4.

    Not the same number

    When both are defined, L ≤ H, but they need not be equal: H("abc", "bca") = 3 while L("abc", "bca") = 2 (delete the a and add it at the end). Both distances passed the metric tests on thousands of random strings.

    Find two strings of the same length whose Levenshtein distance is much smaller than their Hamming distance.

    Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
